_meta.scale: All weights are in units of the spec's primary stat (1.00 = one point of it).
_meta.formula: score = ( SUM(stat_value * weight) * armorClass[itemArmourType] + dps * dpsWeight + procPoints ). The armorClass multiplier is applied ONLY to the eight slots that have an armour class: Head, Shoulder, Chest, Wrist, Hands, Waist, Legs, Feet.
_meta.armorNote: Armour class is a per-spec MULTIPLIER on the final score, never a filter, so a big enough stat upgrade still wins -- which is what lets Holy take cloth. See the armorClass table on each spec. This was documented long before it was implemented; until it was wired in, Hunter and Rogue tier 3 outranked Paladin tier 2. It applies only to the eight true armour slots; Back, Neck, Finger, Trinket and Ranged have no armour class (every class wears the same cloth cloak), and applying the Cloth figure to a cloak printed cloak scores five times too small. Ranking-neutral: 3,230 paladin bands re-scored with the fix, zero changed top-3.
_meta.noLevelScaling: There is NO level scaling on any weight. An earlier version multiplied rating stats by 70/playerLevel on the grounds that a rating point buys more percent at low level. True, but the relative value of a primary stat point rises even faster down there, so scaling only the ratings left them badly overvalued below 60 -- it valued 5 spell crit rating at roughly 4 Strength for a level 13 Retribution paladin, against a real figure near 0.25.
_meta.procNote: Proc value is added in the same points currency by procs.py: damage -> dps -> x dpsWeight; stat buff -> stat x uptime x that stat's weight; mitigation -> effective HP -> x stamina weight / 10. Every scenario constant is named at the top of that file and is an estimate, not sim output. An ON-USE effect is charged once per its stated cooldown (once per engagement if no cooldown is stated), NOT at the 2/minute default used for on-hit procs -- a 30-minute engineering nuke was otherwise priced as a permanent damage source. A quest-scripted effect ('Use: Use on <NPC>...') is worth nothing at all.
_meta.level60Note: At exactly level 60 the picks come from Wowhead's Classic BiS guides, not from these weights. A TBC-only item may displace a guide entry only by beating the guide's own top pick by 20%. These weights therefore do not determine level 60.
_meta.dualWieldNote: A one-hander (InventoryType 13) is a candidate for BOTH hands, with the weapon-damage half of its score halved in the off hand (Dual Wield penalty); stats and procs count fully. Holding any weapon in the off hand requires the Dual Wield skill: warrior 20, rogue 10, hunter 20, no other class ever. Below that level the off hand is a shield.

levelling_1_9.label: Levels 1-9 (no talents yet - shared by all three specs)

PALADIN._dpsWeightNote: Retribution 4.31 and levelling 4.31 are derived from mechanics: 1 Strength = 2 AP = 0.232 dps for a paladin, so 1 weapon dps = 1/0.232 = 4.31 Strength. Holy 0.086 follows the same ratio off its near-zero Strength weight. Protection is the exception: the same derivation gave 2.37, which put pure-DPS Naxxramas one-hand swords (The Hungering Cold, Gressil, Andonisus) at the top of the tank weapon list. A tank's threat comes overwhelmingly from Holy damage -- Seal and Judgement of Righteousness, Consecration, Holy Shield -- which scales off spell power and attack power, not weapon dps, so the ratio does not transfer. Swept 0.0 to 2.37 against Wowhead's Classic Naxxramas tank BiS guide; 0.0 and 0.5 tie for best agreement and 0.5 is chosen as the physically non-zero end of that tie.
PALADIN._weightProvenance: Ordinal priorities taken from Icy Veins TBC Classic stat-priority pages for each spec, then adapted for LEVELLING rather than raiding. That adaptation matters: the published priorities are for level-70 raiding, where hit-to-9%-cap, expertise and armour penetration dominate. Levelling gear from 1-69 carries almost none of those stats and the caps are irrelevant, so raw Strength, weapon damage and survivability stay ahead of them here. These are ordinal-derived, NOT sim-derived, and are the part of this model most worth Henrik's judgement -- editable live in the review page.

WARRIOR._note: Warrior. Arms is two-hand, Fury dual-wields one-handers, Protection is one-hand plus shield. Unlike Paladin there is a real Ranged slot (bows, guns, crossbows, thrown) instead of a relic.
